items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: I was involved with him... I was involved in the Orchestra USA... with the American Jazz Orchestra... Gunther came in one time and we did an Ellington triptych

ctx.x: Yes. Well I called it — I forget what I called it. I can’t remember now. An anxious moment.

Oh yes, we’ve all had many anxious moments. But one, a lot of them involved John Lewis, but well I had anxious moments with Gunther. These are musical things. Well I was involved in the Orchestra USA. One time we had to play a Webern piece. See we were playing all kinds of music. And I’m not really classical, and I had to play the celeste. And this was one of those times where, like the guy with the cymbal, you just count until your — it was just a few little notes I had to play in this spot in this Webern piece.…
I know what you mean. Those orchestra things, man, 86 measures — I’m a saxophone player.
